title: Choose an irrigation backflow preventer from hazard, pressure, elevation, and local rule
description: Separate PVB, RPZ, AVB, anti-siphon, and hose-connection protection for sprinkler systems without assuming one device fits every layout.
answer: Irrigation protection depends on backpressure potential, chemical injection, downstream valves, elevation, continuous pressure, freeze exposure, and what the water authority accepts.
urgency: Fertilizer injection, pumps, high hazard, or backpressure potential can require stronger protection than a simple vacuum breaker.
diagramAlt: Irrigation system comparing elevated PVB, RPZ, AVB, and downstream zones
identifiers: A PVB is raised and testable for applicable backsiphonage conditions.
An RPZ includes a relief zone and broader applicable protection.
An AVB's pressure and downstream-valve limitations must be respected.

choices.label: Raised testable PVB is installed
choices.detail: Use the PVB identification, leak, freeze, and testing route.

choices.label: RPZ with relief opening is installed
choices.detail: Plan drainage, testing, and vent-discharge response.

choices.label: Anti-siphon zone valves are installed
choices.detail: Confirm elevation and non-continuous pressure arrangement.

choices.label: Chemicals or pump pressure are involved
choices.detail: Use the official hazard classification and qualified design route.

steps.title: Map the irrigation system
steps.body: Record supply, pumps, chemical injection, valves, high points, and downstream pressure.

steps.title: Match the protection type
steps.body: Use hazard and pressure conditions plus the accepted local method.

steps.title: Plan freeze and test workflow
steps.body: Winterization, access, annual testing, and report filing can affect the choice.

safeChecks: Photograph the full assembly and zones.
Check the utility's official irrigation rule.
notThisDevice: A sprinkler head check valve is not premise backflow protection.
A hose-bib device is not a whole-irrigation assembly.
A pressure regulator does not replace backflow protection.
evidenceNote: The water authority and manufacturer determine accepted assembly type, testing, winterization, and reporting.
